waiting.title: 8840 Rally Shock n' Roll Racer: the engine's rods and pistons
waiting.what: A correction to the published file, for the V2 engine (function 2: the left rear wheel runs the engine). Each of the two connecting rods should hold its piston by the ball at its end. The file draws each rod’s ball 2 LDU beside its cylinder’s line and each piston about 3.5 LDU above the ball, so neither rod is read as holding its piston: the crankshaft and rods turn, but the pistons stay still. The correction turns each rod a few degrees on the crankshaft’s pin, so its ball lies on its cylinder’s line, and slides each piston down its cylinder onto the ball. Four parts move, by a few LDU each.
waiting.effect: Function 2 goes from partly working to working: the pistons pump as the wheel turns. The set’s other functions are as before.
waiting.confidence: High. A rod’s ball always sits in its piston; the correction keeps each rod on the crankshaft’s pin and each piston in its cylinder, and only closes the gap. The booklet’s step 9 builds the engine so.

waiting.title: 8258 Crane Truck: the joint under the lower boom's actuator
waiting.what: A correction to the published file, for the lower boom (function 3). The boom's actuator takes its drive from the upright axle in the middle of the turntable through a universal joint at its foot. The booklet builds the actuator upright and drops the joint's free end straight onto that axle (step 156); the boom tilts the actuator later and the joint bends. The file draws the joint straight along the tilted actuator, so its free end points 25° away from the axle and nothing is in it. The correction turns that one part, the joint's free end, 25° on the pin it swings on, so the axle goes into it. Nothing else moves.
waiting.effect: The upright axle then drives the joint, the actuator's input and its screw. Function 3 works once its entry also sets the first yellow lever (catch p166 moved +0.4, the other way from function 5's), which the drive to that axle needs: with both, the actuator slides 0.61 LDU and the boom 4.0 LDU a radian of the motor. With either alone it stays partly working. Nothing else in the set changes. The lever set first is a change to our function list; your sign-off of this item covers both the correction to the file and that list change.
waiting.confidence: High. A universal joint's end always sits on its axle; the axle's tip ends where the end's hole starts. Step 156 shows the end going onto the axle.

waiting.title: 42077 Rally Car: a rear half shaft's inner ball
waiting.what: A correction to the published file, for the V6 engine (function 2: pushing the car runs the engine). Each rear wheel is driven from the differential by a half shaft with a ball joint at each end. Both half shafts slope down to the wheels. On one side the file draws the inner ball level while its axle slopes, so the axle misses the ball's hole and that half shaft isn't joined to the differential. The correction tilts that one ball to the same slope as the rest of its half shaft, in its socket. Nothing else moves.
waiting.effect: Function 2 goes from partly working to working: the differential and the engine turn as the car rolls. The set's other functions are as before.
waiting.confidence: High. The ball is the same part as on the other side, which the file draws sloped; step 19 builds each half shaft straight.

waiting.title: 42078 Mack Anthem: the rear crane's actuator axle
waiting.what: A correction to the published file, for the cranes' legs (function 9: one gear at the trailer's rear works both cranes' big actuators). The drive runs from the rear crane along the trailer to the front crane. The two cranes are mirror images, but both use one copy of the actuator's sub-assembly, not mirrored. In the front crane its long axle sits right, held at both ends. In the rear crane the same axle sits 40 LDU too far back, so it misses the connector that passes the drive on to the front crane. The correction moves that axle 40 LDU along itself, in the rear crane only. Nothing else moves, and the front crane is as before. Kinebrick's corrections can now change one use of a sub-assembly that a file places more than once.
waiting.effect: The front crane's actuator is then driven, as the rear one is (each slides 1.6 LDU a turn of the gear, in radians). Function 9 still stays partly working, for another reason: the legs' rack housings don't move as the actuators push. The set's other functions are as before.
waiting.confidence: High. The front crane, built the same way, shows where the axle goes, and steps 142 and 143 put a connector on each end of it.

waiting.title: 42096 Porsche 911 RSR: the rear half shafts' outer ends
waiting.what: A correction to the published file, for the flat six (function 1: pushing the car runs the engine). Each rear wheel is driven from the differential by a half shaft: two ball joints on a short axle. In the file each shaft's outer ball is drawn 20 LDU short of its wheel hub, with the axle half pulled out of it, so the wheels turn nothing. The correction slides each outer ball 20 LDU along its shaft into the hub, the axle fully in it, as step 11 builds it. Two parts move, one on each side.
waiting.effect: Function 1 goes from partly working to working: the differential and the engine turn as the car rolls. The set's other functions are as before.
waiting.confidence: High. With the axle fully in both balls, the shaft is exactly as long as the space from the differential to the hub, and points straight at the hub's socket.
